June: Midsummer Riding

June delivers the longest days of the year — at midsummer, northern Scotland barely gets dark. The riding potential is enormous. But June also marks the start of peak tourist season, and in Scotland, the arrival of the dreaded midge.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 12-20°C. Southern England can reach 25°C+. Scottish Highlands typically 12-18°C.
  • Daylight: Up to 18 hours in Scotland, 16.5 hours in southern England. You can ride from 5am to 10pm.
  • Weather: Generally warm and pleasant, but June can surprise with cold fronts and heavy rain. Don't be complacent.

June Highlights

  • Summer solstice (June 21): The longest day. Plan a dawn-to-dusk ride for maximum daylight miles.
  • TT Isle of Man: The TT races typically fall in late May/early June. If you're planning to attend, book ferries and accommodation months in advance.
  • Wildflower meadows: The Yorkshire Dales hay meadows are at their most colourful in June.
  • Still waters: June often brings calm conditions that turn lochs and lakes into mirrors. Early morning is the best time.

Scottish Midge Alert

From mid-June onwards, Highland midges become active. These tiny biting insects can make outdoor stops miserable if you're unprepared:

  • Carry Smidge or Avon Skin So Soft insect repellent
  • A midge head net weighs nothing and saves your sanity
  • Midges are worst in still, humid conditions near water. A breeze disperses them.
  • They're active dawn and dusk — ride through these times rather than stopping.

Where to Ride in June

  • Northern Scotland: Make the most of the extraordinary daylight. The NC500 in June offers 18 hours of rideable light.
  • Welsh mountains: Warm enough for t-shirt riding in the valleys, cool and fresh on the passes.
  • Channel Islands: June is one of the best months for Channel Islands touring — warm, sunny, and before peak holiday crowds.
June riding in Scotland is special. The sub-Arctic light quality, the endless twilight, and the empty roads in the far north create an atmosphere found nowhere else in Britain. If you've never ridden Scotland in June, put it on your list.

June Touring Strategy

June is ideal for the ambitious tours you've been planning all winter. With 16-18 hours of daylight, you can cover serious ground without rushing. A Scotland loop taking in Glencoe, Torridon, and the NC500 is achievable in a week and represents the pinnacle of UK motorcycle touring.

If Scotland isn't on the agenda, June is also excellent for the Channel Islands — Condor Ferries run their summer schedule, the islands are warm and sunny, and the compact riding on Guernsey and Jersey makes for a unique touring experience completely different from mainland Britain.
keyTakeaways: June brings the longest days: up to 18 hours of daylight in Scotland, letting you ride 5am to 10pm.
Temperatures average 12-20C, with southern England reaching 25C-plus and the Highlands 12-18C.
The summer solstice on 21 June is ideal for a dawn-to-dusk maximum-daylight ride.
Highland midges become active from mid-June, so carry Smidge or Avon Skin So Soft and a head net.
Northern Scotland and the NC500 are exceptional in June thanks to the extraordinary sub-Arctic light.

faq.q: What makes June riding special in the UK?
faq.a: June delivers the longest days of the year, and at midsummer northern Scotland barely gets dark. That means up to 18 hours of daylight in Scotland and 16.5 hours in southern England, so you can ride from 5am to 10pm. The sub-Arctic light quality, endless twilight and empty roads in the far north create an atmosphere found nowhere else in Britain.

faq.q: When do Scottish midges become a problem in June?
faq.a: From mid-June onwards Highland midges become active and can make outdoor stops miserable. Carry Smidge or Avon Skin So Soft repellent and pack a midge head net, which weighs nothing and saves your sanity. Midges are worst in still, humid conditions near water and are active at dawn and dusk, so ride through those times rather than stopping.

faq.q: How can I make the most of the summer solstice?
faq.a: The solstice on 21 June is the longest day, so plan a dawn-to-dusk ride for maximum daylight miles. A route from an east-facing sunrise viewpoint, west through the day, to a west-facing sunset location keeps the light in your favour. In the far north around Durness and Cape Wrath the sky glows through a brief twilight, creating a uniquely beautiful midnight light.

faq.q: Where should I ride in June?
faq.a: Northern Scotland tops the list, with the NC500 offering 18 hours of rideable light. The Welsh mountains are warm enough for t-shirt riding in the valleys and cool on the passes, and June is one of the best months for the Channel Islands before peak holiday crowds. A week-long Scotland loop taking in Glencoe, Torridon and the NC500 is the pinnacle of UK touring.

faq.q: Is June weather reliable for touring?
faq.a: June is generally warm and pleasant but should not be treated as guaranteed. Cold fronts and heavy rain can still appear, so do not be complacent. Predawn temperatures can sit at 5-8C before rising past 20C by mid-afternoon, so a layering system is essential. Calm June mornings often turn lochs and lakes into mirrors, making early starts especially rewarding.
